slot.brief: Given an infinite GP sum relation like a + ar + … = expression in a, take logs to find the common ratio r.

stem: For $a>0$ and $|r|<1$, if $\log_3(a+ar+ar^2+\cdots)=1+\log_3 a$, then the common ratio $r$ is

verdicts.working: The series sums to \(\frac{a}{1-r}\). Thus \(\log_3\frac{a}{1-r}=1+\log_3 a\), so \(\frac{1}{1-r}=3\) and \(r=\frac23\).

working:
$\log_3\!\left(\dfrac{a}{1-r}\right)=1+\log_3 a=\log_3(3a)$
$\dfrac{a}{1-r}=3a \implies 1-r=\dfrac{1}{3} \implies r=\dfrac{2}{3}$

Independent check: The series sums to \(\frac{a}{1-r}\). Thus \(\log_3\frac{a}{1-r}=1+\log_3 a\), so \(\frac{1}{1-r}=3\) and \(r=\frac23\).
solution:
The infinite geometric series sums to $\frac{a}{1-r}$. Since $1+\log_3 a=\log_3(3a)$,
$$\frac{a}{1-r}=3a \implies r=\frac{2}{3}.$$
